name: Treasury bill laddering
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Short-Term Funding Demand
caseLead: The investment case rests on governments issuing short-dated bills to finance regular spending and central banks maintaining short-term rates to implement monetary policy, allowing a rolling ladder to earn close to the policy rate. The opportunity persists because fiscal funding needs, institutional demand for liquid collateral and geopolitical uncertainty create continuous issuance and trading, while staggered maturities reduce dependence on any single policy decision.
caseRest: The main risk is that rapid policy tightening raises bill yields before existing tranches mature, producing small mark-to-market losses that can temporarily exceed accrued income. A sustained cutting cycle also reduces returns because each maturing tranche must be reinvested at a lower yield, although existing bills record modest price gains. Inflation is the larger economic risk because it can reduce real income even when nominal returns remain positive and monthly volatility stays low.
figNote: The large figure on each card shows the upper bound of the Federal Reserve’s target rate at the end of the episode. This rate anchors Treasury bill yields, so a higher figure generally increases ladder income after maturing tranches have been reinvested.

events.title: Fed cuts rates to the effective floor
events.text: The Federal Reserve cut rates to near zero as the financial crisis reduced credit and economic activity. Existing bills gained as yields fell, but subsequent maturities were reinvested at much lower rates.

events.title: Debt ceiling distorts near-term bill prices
events.text: The US debt ceiling dispute and sovereign downgrade increased demand for safe assets while raising concern around selected maturity dates. Results were mixed because most bills gained, but securities exposed to payment delays briefly weakened.

events.title: Pandemic flight lifts Treasury bill prices
events.text: The global rush for liquidity pushed investors into Treasury bills as the Federal Reserve cut rates and expanded market support. The ladder gained from falling yields and strong demand, although its future income declined sharply.

events.title: Ukraine invasion supports demand for bills
events.text: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine increased demand for liquid government securities, supporting bill prices. Gains remained limited because high inflation kept the Federal Reserve on course to begin raising rates in March.

events.title: Inflation repricing drives the worst monthly fall
events.text: The Federal Reserve delivered another 75 basis point increase as persistent inflation lifted expected policy rates. Existing bills fell slightly before maturity, producing the ladder’s worst monthly loss, while later reinvestment secured higher income.

events.title: Debt ceiling raises yields on specific bills
events.text: The US debt ceiling dispute raised yields on bills maturing near the projected cash exhaustion date. The ladder was mixed because exposed tranches weakened, while other maturities retained safe-haven demand and generated strong carry.

instrument: US Treasury bills; one to four months to maturity; one tranche rolled every four weeks
rules: Equal maturity buckets maintained across the ladder; proceeds reinvested at maturity; bills normally held to redemption
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads and auction or brokerage fees deducted at each reinvestment
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from policy rate income to maturity diversification

legs.purpose: Earns short-rate income with limited duration
Locks in income across policy meetings
Extends income while limiting price risk

entry: Each tranche entered at auction or in the secondary market after the preceding tranche matures
size: Equal capital allocated across four maturity buckets
exit: Each bill held to maturity and its proceeds reinvested at the longest ladder point
stop: No price stop; exposure reduced only if settlement or payment risk becomes material
marketWatch: Policy guidance, overnight index swaps and Treasury auction demand indicate the income available when each tranche is reinvested. Inflation releases and central bank meetings matter because unexpected tightening can cause small price losses, while rate cuts reduce future income. Fiscal deadlines also matter when payment concerns affect specific bill maturities.

favourable.heading: High stable policy rates
favourable.text: High and stable rates favour the strategy because each maturing tranche is reinvested at an attractive yield without material losses on existing bills. The 2023 to 2024 period followed this pattern after the Federal Reserve completed most of its tightening cycle.

favourable.heading: Gradual rate increases
favourable.text: Gradual tightening favours the ladder because short maturities limit price declines while frequent reinvestment raises portfolio income. During the measured increases of 2017 and 2018, higher coupon accrual broadly offset the small mark-to-market effect.

favourable.heading: Flight to government liquidity
favourable.text: A flight to liquidity favours the strategy because demand for Treasury bills pushes yields lower and raises the value of existing tranches. In March 2020, bills gained as investors sought cash-like government securities and the Federal Reserve cut rates rapidly.

adverse.heading: Rapid unexpected tightening
adverse.text: Rapid tightening hurts the strategy because bill yields rise before accrued income can offset the decline in existing prices. In September 2022, persistent inflation and a 75 basis point Federal Reserve increase produced the backtest’s worst monthly fall.

adverse.heading: Early sustained rate cuts
adverse.text: Sustained easing reduces income because each maturing tranche must be reinvested at a lower yield, outweighing the brief price gain on existing bills. After the emergency cuts of 2020, ladder income remained close to zero until policy tightening began in 2022.

adverse.heading: Debt ceiling maturity distortions
adverse.text: Debt ceiling disputes hurt exposed tranches because investors demand additional yield on bills that may mature near a payment deadline. In May 2023, yields on selected June maturities rose even as other Treasury bills retained strong safe-haven demand.

infoHist: Historical results show the ladder’s estimated total return during each event, including accrued income, changes in bill prices and reinvestment at maturity. Returns use equal allocations across the four maturity buckets and deduct estimated trading costs.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated return over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn’s scenario engine projects changes in Federal Reserve expectations, Treasury bill yields and maturity-specific liquidity premiums, which are then applied to the ladder’s existing tranches and scheduled reinvestments.
